history.sg_progress: The key roles and responsibilities related to central and local ICT security functions have been incorporated into the ICT accountability framework, which is under review prior to its final approval. III. Status of implementation of recommendations on the Umoja system In annex II to its report on the United Nations for the year ended 31 December 2024, the Board provided a summary of the status of implementation of its 17 extant recommendations on the Umoja system relating to prior periods. Of the 17 extant recommendations, 12 (70 per cent) had been implemented, 3 (18 per cent) had been overtaken by events and the other 2 (12 per cent) were under implementation. Table 5 presents a summary of the overall situation as of August 2025 with respect to the two recommendations that were determined by the Board to be under implementation as of December 2024. Of those outstanding recommendations, one is scheduled to be implemented in 2025 and the other in 2026. history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration clearly define the scope of ICT security, including key central and local roles and responsibilities in the ICT accountability framework as part of the ICT governance structure, and ensure that they are properly implemented.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The ICT accountability framework was approved at the ICT Steering Committee meeting on 7 May 2026. Section 3 of the endorsed ICT accountability framework lays out the specific roles and responsibilities held centrally by the Chief Information Technology Officer and section 4 sets out the responsibilities of heads of entities. These include the roles and responsibilities for ICT security. Annex 1 of the ICT accountability framework provides a further breakdown of roles and responsibilities for ICT security based on the ICT entity type, as follows: Central services of the Office of Information and Communications Technology: develop, maintain and promulgate ICT security policies, standards, awareness and operational resilience frameworks; perform security assessments; report security incidents; support and coordinate responses to incidents as appropriate; coordinate ICT security-specific activities across the Secretariat; provide guidance on ICT security matters. ICT service provider entities: implement ICT security requirements and perform ICT security operations including implementing and maintaining approved controls, in line with promulgated policies and standards; report and respond to incidents as applicable; maintain an ICT focal point function. ICT embedded entities: implement ICT security requirements and perform ICT security operations including implementing and maintaining approved controls, in line with promulgated policies and standards; report and respond to incidents as applicable; maintain an ICT focal point function. ICT supported entities: adhere to ICT security operational requirements in line with promulgated policies and standards and report incidents as applicable; ensure that an ICT security focal point assumes responsibility. The endorsed ICT accountability framework defines the scope of ICT security, including key central and local roles and responsibilities, as part of the ICT governance structure, which will also come under the monitoring of the framework outlined in the document.
history.board_assessment: Given that the accountability framework has been reviewed by the ICT Steering Committee and was released in May 2026, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
